A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOP-ERL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison after matching the shifted appendix pages.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments on MetaWorld, Hopper Jump, and Box Pushing, together with ablations and appendix analyses (Figures 4–9 and 12; Table 1).

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulation results and supplementary analyses, including benchmark learning curves, critic-update comparisons, and action-correlation visualizations.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 and Appendix A.1 explicitly enforce segment-specific initial conditions during policy updates. v4 instead specifies task-initial conditions for policy updates and reserves segment-specific enforcement for critic training (A.1/B.4). This locally revises the reported update procedure; the architecture and overall objectives remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 50 MetaWorld tasks, Hopper Jump, and dense- and sparse-reward Box Pushing. Appendix task descriptions, randomized Box Pushing conditions, and supplementary task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain BBRL, TCE, PPO, SAC, gSDE, PINK, and GTrXL trained with PPO (Figures 4, 8–9; Table 3). The critic-update variants compared in Figure 5 and Table 1 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The MetaWorld endpoint-success rule repeated in v4 Appendix C.2 was already specified in v2 Section 5.2. Benchmark budgets, model configurations, preprocessing settings, and hyperparameters in Tables 4–7 are unchanged. No separate evaluation-protocol revision is documented.

E4.justification: Appendices A.1/B.4 add a qualitative comparison of task-initial versus segment-specific initialization for policy updates and distinguish its effects from critic training. No new quantitative ablation table or curve accompanies this comparison; the existing Section 5.3 ablations and Appendix D correlation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight random seeds, interquartile means, and 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals in Section 5. No additional run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results, benchmark curves, and Table 1 entries are unchanged. v4 Appendix A.1 newly reports that task-initial conditions yield better policy-update performance than segment-specific conditions, with B.4 distinguishing benefits for critic learning from difficulties for policy updates. This is an added qualitative finding, not a demonstrated performance gain between versions.

T1.justification: The N-step-return reasoning, trust-region formulation, and movement-primitive ODE and initial-condition derivations remain unchanged. The initialization revision changes how the method uses the existing formulas; no new theoretical result or derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about transformer-based off-policy ERL, sequence-value learning, sample efficiency, and performance across 53 tasks.

C2.justification: v4 explains that segment-specific initialization can hinder policy updates because those conditions are not supplied to the policy, despite improving consistency for the critic. Appendices A.1/B.4 qualify the usefulness of enforcement and identify this issue for future investigation. The existing limitations concerning replanning and POMDPs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract's code hyperlink changes from a direct GitHub repository to a project webpage, revising the documented access route. Hyperparameter Tables 4–7 and the reproducibility statement remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the destination's contents or availability.

R1.justification: The reference list and research positioning are unchanged. The added MetaWorld appendix paragraph repeats citations to Otto et al. (2022) and Li et al. (2024) already used for the same protocol in Section 5.2.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to Section 4.4 and Appendices A.1/B.4, an expanded MetaWorld explanation in C.2, and small footnote and funding-acknowledgment edits. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Local reflow shifts appendix material and produces a sparsely filled continuation page for C.2, moving subsequent figures and tables one page later. Existing graphics, captions, and table structures are preserved without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 replaces v2's policy-update enforcement instruction with an explicit distinction between policy and critic initialization, and explains the associated conditioning difficulty (A.1/B.4). This makes the intended procedure and its tradeoff clearer. The gain is limited: the new performance comparison is unquantified, existing numerical evidence is unchanged, and the MetaWorld addition largely repeats an already documented rule.
